text: The author page explicitly describes the value-weighted and equal-weighted bias estimates as estimates for buy-and-hold portfolios. The weighting scheme is part of the reported result. (low confidence)
keywords: Point-in-time crypto universe liquidity and survivorship screening

text: The SSRN abstract and author page for Ammann, Burdorf, Liebi and Stöckl's Survivorship and Delisting Bias in Cryptocurrency Markets report a sample of 3,904 cryptocurrencies from 2014–2021 and estimated annualized bias of 0.93% for value-weighted portfolios and 62.19% for equal-weighted portfolios. The two pages describe the same study. (low confidence)
keywords: Point-in-time crypto universe liquidity and survivorship screening

text: Cong, Li, Tang and Yang's NBER working paper tests 29 exchanges using data from July to November 2019 and estimates wash trading averaged over 70% of reported volume on the unregulated exchanges in its sample. Separately, Coin Metrics describes a Trusted Exchange Framework that vets data quality before calculating market metrics and selecting index constituents. (medium confidence)
keywords: Point-in-time crypto universe liquidity and survivorship screening

text: CoinMarketCap describes its Liquidity Score as simulated immediate buy and sell slippage over order sizes from about $100 to $200,000, with greater weight on $100–$10,000 orders. S&P Global separately evaluates market volume, bid-ask spread, depth and slippage, and its report table gives mean 1% total Binance depth of EUR 0.40 million for EUR-USDC, EUR 1.00 million for BTC-EUR and EUR 31.10 million for BTC-USDT. These figures describe that report's sample. (medium confidence)
keywords: Point-in-time crypto universe liquidity and survivorship screening

text: CoinMarketCap describes its Liquidity Score as a purely quantitative measure using exchange API order books or exchange submissions, refreshed every two hours subject to order-book data availability. S&P separately describes cumulative bid-side and ask-side depth for a specified date and reports few executable Kraken USDC-USD trades within 1% of the peg in its March 2023 Silicon Valley Bank crisis example; it says participants might have been more willing to buy larger orders at the 10% level. These are provider descriptions and report examples. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-08)
keywords: Point-in-time crypto universe liquidity and survivorship screening

text: Wash-trading estimates in the reviewed sources depend on estimator and coverage. Cong, Li, Tang and Yang report over 70% for their main unregulated-exchange estimate, about 61% after exchange-characteristic controls, and 16.3 percent for an alternative Benford-based estimate; they explain that the Benford method misses some wash trading. Coin Metrics calls Trusted Volume a lower-bound estimate that excludes DEXes and uncovered centralized exchanges, and warns that calculating an overall fake-volume percentage can give misleading conclusions. (medium confidence)
keywords: Point-in-time crypto universe liquidity and survivorship screening

text: The same study's SSRN abstract reports that a survival-conditioned sample overestimates its size premium by 50%. After controlling for survivorship and delisting bias, the abstract reports no evidence of a positive relationship between average returns and one-week momentum, market beta or downside risk. (low confidence)
keywords: Point-in-time crypto universe liquidity and survivorship screening

text: Concretum's tutorial describes using CoinMarketCap's historical OHLCV endpoint to retrieve daily open, high, low, close, volume and market cap by numeric coin ID. It presents a download workflow including active and defunct projects and warns that full execution can exceed 20 hours because of rate limits. These are the tutorial's stated data fields and execution warning. (low confidence)

text: Cong, Li, Tang and Yang limit their wash-trading transaction sample to BTC, ETH, XRP and LTC, and the paper treats cryptocurrency-USD and cryptocurrency-USDT pairs as the same. Those are explicit sample and quote-currency conventions of this study. (low confidence)

text: Concretum's dataset tutorial describes CoinMarketCap's numeric UCID as a persistent identifier rather than a ticker, including across branding changes or delistings. Gimmer separately warns that the same ticker need not identify the same asset or contract and recommends recording venue, base, quote, symbol and listing or removal history. (medium confidence)

text: For a removed market, Gimmer recommends retaining it through its last eligible timestamp and explicitly stating how an open position is handled, rather than silently deleting that record from the historical test. (low confidence)

text: Gimmer explicitly advises against treating every delisted asset as a total loss: it distinguishes removal, rename, migration and data loss, and calls for verified market history and an explicit open-position rule rather than assigning zero value or a successful exit without evidence. keywords: Point-in-time crypto universe liquidity and survivorship screening

text: CoinAPI's survivorship article describes a point-in-time universe as the tradable universe at the historical selection date, including markets that later become inactive or delisted and using information available by that date. Gimmer similarly recommends date-specific eligibility and retention of removed markets through the last eligible observation. (medium confidence)
keywords: Point-in-time crypto universe liquidity and survivorship screening

text: Gimmer recommends applying liquidity, trading-history, price and other selection filters using information available at the selection timestamp, and warns that current market capitalization or present-day volume reintroduces future knowledge. CoinAPI likewise recommends a point-in-time universe and signals restricted to information available at that date. (medium confidence)
keywords: Point-in-time crypto universe liquidity and survivorship screening

text: CoinAPI lists delisted pairs, changed symbol conventions, expired derivatives and venue shutdowns as sources of crypto survivorship bias. Gimmer separately warns against silently merging renamed assets and recommends verifying identity and conversion boundaries. (medium confidence)
keywords: Point-in-time crypto universe liquidity and survivorship screening

text: Gimmer's proposed selection-log workflow records each rebalance timestamp and market identity, applies contemporaneous filters, classifies exclusion reasons, and freezes the eligible set before strategy tuning. It recommends labeling a survivor-only sensitivity check as using later survival knowledge. These are the article's methodological recommendations. (low confidence)
keywords: Point-in-time crypto universe liquidity and survivorship screening

text: CoinAPI's survivorship article describes separate active-symbol and historical-symbol endpoints with pagination and proposes combining their lists with coverage timestamps for a historical-universe workflow. Its data_start/data_end glossary says those fields are dataset-coverage bounds, not authoritative listing/delisting dates or a guarantee of continuous observations; coverage can begin after listing or end before delisting. The glossary says active-symbol data_end can move and recommends recording the metadata snapshot timestamp. These are provider descriptions, without verified endpoint execution or a demonstrated complete historical venue universe. (low confidence)
keywords: Point-in-time crypto universe liquidity and survivorship screening
